## What Was Claimed

The pnpm selector `--filter-prod` was allegedly omitted from selector detection, allowing `pnpm --filter-prod web test` to pass preflight against the root package and execute in another workspace.

## What We Found

The frozen base contains no selector allowlist or `packageSelectionOption` helper. `packageScriptName` rejects every package-manager invocation whose first argument starts with `-`. Therefore `pnpm --filter-prod web test` reaches `unsupportedPackageManagerOptionsError` and cannot pass preflight. Existing focused coverage tests npm selectors but does not name pnpm `--filter-prod`, so a direct regression case is still warranted.

## Root Cause

The source finding describes an earlier implementation. By frozen base `0b7fcd2c596e05d7a98e57a4464d39aae987f71d`, package-manager option handling had been generalized to fail closed before script inference, eliminating the cited omission.

## Affected Files

- `src/adapters/verification-preflight.ts` — current generic fail-closed package-manager option handling.
- `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts` — focused selector regression suite lacks the exact pnpm case.

## Evidence

- `packageScriptName` throws whenever `argv[1].startsWith("-")` for npm, pnpm, yarn, or bun.
- No `packageSelectionOption`, selector list, or `--filter` token exists under `src/`.
- Existing test coverage enumerates npm selector forms but not `pnpm --filter-prod web test`.

## History Findings

Issue #196 was created from correctness finding `correctness-argv-3` on PR #192 at head `d731df0c59a6c3bd3b36fcde512c759ab6625ae0`. The current frozen integration base instead uses generalized rejection, so the cited implementation is stale relative to this run.

## Recommendation

Add the exact pnpm `--filter-prod` invocation to focused preflight regression coverage without changing production logic. This proves the current fail-closed invariant and prevents reintroduction of an incomplete selector list.

## Related Issues

- Source issue `#111`
- Source PR `#192`

## Decomposition Assessment

No decomposition is required. The remaining work is one focused test update.

## Acceptance Spec

- [ ] `pnpm --filter-prod web test` is rejected as an unsupported package-manager option.
- [ ] The regression uses an available pnpm fixture executable so rejection exercises option validation, not executable lookup.
- [ ] Required repository check passes.
- [ ] Fresh correctness and security reviewers approve the frozen remediation head.

<!-- INVESTIGATION:COMPLETE -->

## Builder Contract

### Objective

Lock in fail-closed handling for pnpm `--filter-prod` by adding the exact reported invocation to verification-preflight regression coverage.

### Allowed Paths

- `test/adapters/verification-preflight.test.ts`

### Forbidden Changes

- Do not change production preflight behavior.
- Do not change verification policy, command execution, workflow authority, schemas, or GitHub artifacts.
- Do not add dependencies or broaden package-manager support.

### Invariants

- Package-manager options remain unsupported for tracked verification.
- Rejection must occur after executable availability succeeds, proving option validation owns the failure.
- Existing npm selector regressions remain intact.

### Deliverables

- An executable pnpm fixture alongside the existing npm fixture.
- A focused `pnpm --filter-prod web test` regression case.
- Passing required `check` verification.
- Fresh correctness and security review of the committed head.

### Acceptance Mapping

| Check | Implementation |
|---|---|
| `AC-1` | Add `pnpm --filter-prod web test` to the malformed-root selector table and assert unsupported options. |
| `AC-2` | Create an executable `pnpm` shim in the fixture PATH. |
| `AC-3` | Run bound verification command `check`. |
| `AC-4` | Prepare the PR and run the required fresh reviewer panel. |

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT -->
## Implementation Context

### History

The finding originated on PR #192 at head `d731df0c59a6c3bd3b36fcde512c759ab6625ae0`. Frozen base `0b7fcd2c596e05d7a98e57a4464d39aae987f71d` already replaced selector enumeration with generic rejection.

### Callers And Data Flow

`preflightRequiredVerificationCommands` resolves the executable, then `packageScriptName` classifies supported managers and rejects a leading option before package-script lookup. The test must supply pnpm on PATH to reach that branch.

### CI Surface

The required bound command is `npm run check`, covering TypeScript compilation and all Node tests.

### Prior Findings

The original high-severity production-safety concern was workspace selection escaping the configured cwd/package-script binding. Current source is safe; explicit regression coverage is absent.

### Hazards

A missing pnpm fixture would produce a false-positive test that only validates executable lookup. Production code changes would exceed the validated scope.

<!-- FORGE:CONTEXT:COMPLETE -->

<!-- FORGE:ARCHITECT -->
## Implementation Plan

1. Extend the test fixture to create an executable `pnpm` shim.
2. Add the exact `pnpm --filter-prod web test` argv to the malformed-root selector regression table.
3. Run required `check` verification and create the implementation commit.
4. Prepare review and run fresh correctness and security reviewers against the frozen head.

### Out Of Scope

- Supporting package-manager selectors.
- Refactoring preflight parsing.
- Changing verification command execution or policy.
